subject: chemistry
label: 2022 Sem 1
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Select the correct option for each question. No writing is allowed during the first 10 minutes, which are for reading the paper.

concepts: trend of ionization potential across Period 3
questions.question: In the Periodic Table, elements of Period 3 are arranged in the increasing order of ionization potential as:
questions.solution: Option (b) Mg, Si, S, Ar. Ionization energy generally increases across period 3 because of increasing nuclear charge while shielding stays relatively the same. Correct order: Mg, Si, S, Ar.

questions.question: If Relative Molecular Mass of Butane (C4H10) is 58 then, its vapour density will be:
questions.solution: Option (b) 29. Molecular mass = 2 x vapour density; 58 = 2 x VD, so VD = 58/2 = 29.

questions.question: Identify one statement that holds true for electrolysis of molten lead bromide:

options.a: Silver grey metal deposits at the anode.
options.b: Temperature is not maintained during the electrolysis.
options.c: Brown vapours of bromine are obtained at the anode.
options.d: Electrolyte contains H+ ions along with Pb2+ ions.

questions.solution: Option (c) Brown vapours of bromine are obtained at the anode.. At anode: 2Br- -> Br2 + 2e- (reddish brown vapours). At cathode: Pb2+ + 2e- -> Pb. So brown vapour of bromine is obtained at the anode.

questions.question: The tendency of an atom to attract shared pair of electrons to itself when forming a chemical bond is known as:
questions.solution: Option (b) Electronegativity. Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself in a chemical bond.

concepts: ionic solids do not conduct: no free ions
questions.question: Solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity as:

options.a: The strength of the bond is weak.
options.c: It does not contain any free ions.
options.d: It contains free ions as well as molecules.

questions.solution: Option (c) It does not contain any free ions.. Solid NaCl has a closely packed structure with strong electrostatic forces; its ions are immobile, i.e. it has no free ions, so it cannot conduct electricity.

questions.question: Elements A and B have atomic numbers 8 and 13 respectively. The chemical formula formed between A and B will be:
questions.solution: Option (d) B2A3. A (8) has 6 valence electrons and forms A2-; B (13) has 3 valence electrons and forms B3+. Criss-cross gives B2A3.

questions.question: The percentage of hydrogen present in NaOH is: (Relative Molecular Mass of NaOH = 40) (At. Wt. of H = 1)

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question: A salt formed by incomplete neutralisation of an acid by a base:
questions.solution: Option (b) Acid salt. A salt formed by incomplete neutralisation of an acid by a base is an acid salt (contains replaceable hydrogen), e.g. NaHCO3, NaHSO4.

concepts: Fe(OH)3 reddish brown precipitate with NaOH
questions.question: The colour of the precipitate formed after the addition of a small amount of sodium hydroxide solution to an aqueous solution of ferric chloride is:
questions.solution: Option (c) reddish brown. FeCl3 + 3NaOH -> Fe(OH)3 (reddish brown ppt) + 3NaCl. (Printed explanation wrongly calls it ferrous hydroxide; it is ferric hydroxide.)

concepts: alkaline earth metals have 2 valence electrons
questions.question: Alkaline earth metals have the same:
questions.solution: Option (a) number of valence electrons. Alkaline earth metals (Group 2) all have 2 valence electrons. (No printed key; answer from subject knowledge. Question marked out of syllabus.)

concepts: covalent non-electrolyte (CCl4) does not ionise in water
questions.question: Which of the following compounds neither dissociate nor ionise in water?
questions.solution: Option (d) Carbon tetrachloride. Carbon tetrachloride is a non-polar covalent compound with no ions; it neither dissociates nor ionises in water.

questions.question:
The table shows the electronic configuration of four elements.
Element | Electronic configuration
W | 2, 6
X | 2, 8
Y | 2, 8, 1
Z | 2, 8, 7
Which pair of atoms will form a covalent compound?

options.c: an atom of W and an atom of X
options.d: an atom of Y and an atom of Z

questions.solution: Option (a) two atoms of W. Covalent bonds form by sharing electrons. Two atoms of W (2,6) each need 2 electrons and share them (O2). X is a noble gas (inert); Y is an alkali metal and with Z forms an ionic compound.

questions.question: Element with an atomic number 19 will:

options.a: accept an electron and get oxidised
options.b: accept an electron and get reduced
options.c: lose an electron and get oxidised
options.d: lose an electron and get reduced

questions.solution: Option (c) lose an electron and get oxidised. Atomic number 19 (potassium, 2,8,8,1) loses one electron to form K+; loss of electrons is oxidation. (No printed key; answer from subject knowledge.)

concepts: lone pairs in water, ammonia, methane, ammonium ion
questions.question: Which of the following has two sets of lone pair of electrons in them?
questions.solution: Option (c) Water. In water, oxygen has six valence electrons; two are shared with H atoms, leaving two lone pairs.

concepts: empirical to molecular formula, n = molecular mass / empirical mass
questions.question: If the empirical mass of the formula PQ2 is 10 and the Relative Molecular Mass is 30, then the molecular formula will be:
questions.solution: Option (d) P3Q6. n = molecular mass / empirical mass = 30/10 = 3. Molecular formula = (PQ2)3 = P3Q6.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question: Which of the following is a tribasic acid?
questions.solution: Option (c) H3PO4. H3PO4 is tribasic: it can donate all three H+ ions.

concepts: electrochemical series preferential discharge at cathode
questions.question: If a solution of an electrolyte mixture has calcium ions, cupric ions, zinc ions and magnesium ions, which of these ions would you see preferentially discharged at the cathode?
questions.solution: Option (c) Cupric ions. Cupric ions are preferentially discharged (lowest in the electrochemical series): Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu.

questions.question: Which of the following ions will readily discharge at the anode during the electrolysis of acidified water?
questions.solution: Option (a) OH-. OH- ions are preferentially discharged at the anode: 4OH- - 4e- -> 2H2O + O2.

questions.question: If the empirical formula of a compound is CH and its vapour density is 13, then its molecular formula will be: (At. Wt. C = 12, H = 1)
questions.solution: Option (b) C2H2. Molecular mass = 2 x 13 = 26; empirical formula mass = 13; n = 26/13 = 2; molecular formula = (CH)2 = C2H2.

concepts: tetraamminecopper(II) deep blue complex with excess NH4OH
questions.question: Aqueous solution of cupric chloride forms a deep blue solution on addition of:
questions.solution: Option (d) excess ammonium hydroxide. Excess ammonium hydroxide gives a deep blue solution of the tetraamminecopper(II) complex, [Cu(NH3)4]2+.

questions.question: Which statement about conduction of electricity is correct?

options.a: Electricity is conducted in aqueous solution by electrons.
options.b: Electricity is conducted in a metal wire by ions
options.c: Electricity is conducted in a molten electrolyte by electrons.
options.d: Electricity is conducted in an acid solution by ions.

questions.solution: Option (d) Electricity is conducted in an acid solution by ions.. Electrolytes (aqueous, molten, acids) conduct by movement of ions; metals conduct by electrons. (No printed key; answer from subject knowledge.)

questions.question: If an element has low ionization potential, then it is likely to be a:
questions.solution: Option (a) metal. Metals have low ionization potential because they lose electrons easily to form cations.

concepts: electron dot structures of covalent compounds
questions.question: Which electron arrangement for the outer shell electrons in a covalent compound is correct?

options.a: H x. Cl electron-dot structure of HCl (diagram option a)
options.b: H x. Cl electron-dot structure of HCl with extra pairs of electrons drawn (diagram option b)
options.c: N with three H atoms sharing three pairs and a lone pair of electrons on N (NH3) (diagram option c)
options.d: N with three H atoms sharing three pairs and no lone pair on N (diagram option d)

questions.solution: Option (c) N with three H atoms sharing three pairs and a lone pair of electrons on N (NH3) (diagram option c). In nitrogen there are 5 valence electrons; three are shared with three hydrogen atoms and one lone pair remains on nitrogen (NH3).
questions.figure_desc: Four electron dot-and-cross diagrams as the options (HCl and NH3 structures); only the option texts are described here.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question: The products formed when an acid reacts with a base is:
questions.solution: Option (c) salt and water. Neutralisation gives salt and water, e.g. NaOH + HCl -> NaCl + H2O.

questions.question: In the circuit below, the lamp lights up. What could X be?

options.a: a solution of alcohol in water
options.b: a solution of sodium chloride in water

questions.solution: Option (b) a solution of sodium chloride in water. A solution of NaCl dissociates into Na+ and Cl- ions which carry current, so the lamp lights.
questions.figure_desc: Simple circuit with a cell, a lamp and a gap/container holding substance X between two electrodes; lamp lights up.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a non-metallic cation?
questions.solution: Option (b) NH4+. NH4+ (ammonium) is a cation formed from non-metals only. (No printed key; answer from subject knowledge.)

questions.question: Type of bonding present in hydrogen chloride:
questions.solution: Option (c) covalent. Hydrogen and chlorine share an electron pair: covalent bond between two non-metals.

questions.question: The non-metallic properties of elements from left to right in a Periodic Table:
questions.solution: Option (a) increases. Non-metallic character increases from left to right across a period.

concepts: weak electrolyte: acetic acid partial ionisation
questions.question: The aqueous solution that contains both ions and molecules:
questions.solution: Option (c) acetic acid. Acetic acid is a weak electrolyte: it ionises only slightly, so the solution has both ions and molecules; the others are strong electrolytes.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
concepts: basic oxide soluble in water is an alkali (Na2O)
questions.question: The basic oxide which is an alkali:
questions.solution: Option (b) Sodium oxide. Sodium oxide dissolves in water to form hydroxide: Na2O + H2O -> 2NaOH.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
concepts: pH scale: pH 2 is a strong acid
questions.question: If the pH of a solution is '2', then the solution is a:
questions.solution: Option (a) strong acid. pH 2 is a strongly acidic solution.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question: The acidity of aluminium hydroxide is:
questions.solution: Option (a) 3. Al(OH)3 + 3HCl -> AlCl3 + 3H2O; it reacts with 3 H+, so acidity is 3.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
concepts: hydracids contain hydrogen and a non-metal
questions.question: Hydracids are those acids which contain:

options.c: Hydrogen and a non-metal other than oxygen

questions.solution: Option (c) Hydrogen and a non-metal other than oxygen. Hydracids contain hydrogen and a non-metal other than oxygen (e.g. HCl). (No printed key; answer from subject knowledge.)

questions.question: The oxidation reaction among the following is:
questions.solution: Option (b) Fe2+ - 1e- -> Fe3+. Oxidation is loss of electrons: Fe2+ - e- -> Fe3+. The others are gain of electrons (reduction).

concepts: action of excess NaOH on Ca2+, Zn2+, Pb2+ salts
questions.question: A student added excess of sodium hydroxide solution to each of the salt solutions listed below. An insoluble precipitate formed was observed in:
questions.solution: Option (a) Calcium nitrate. Calcium nitrate gives insoluble Ca(OH)2 which does not dissolve in excess NaOH; zinc and lead hydroxides dissolve in excess NaOH, and sodium nitrate gives no precipitate.

concepts: object as cathode and plating metal as anode
questions.question: Which apparatus could be used to electroplate an iron nail with copper?
questions.solution: Option (a). On closing the circuit, copper is deposited on the iron nail (cathode) as Cu ions migrate from the copper anode through the copper salt solution.
questions.figure_desc: Four diagrams of electrolysis cells with different electrodes/electrolytes; the correct one has the iron nail as cathode, copper as anode in copper sulphate solution.

concepts: same group elements C and D
questions.question:
The table below shows the electronic arrangements of six atoms, A to F.
Atom: A, B, C, D, E, F
Electronic configuration: 2,5 | 2 | 2,6 | 2,8,6 | 2,8,8 | 2,8,3
With respect to the table select the following:
(i) Two atoms from the same group of the periodic table:
questions.solution: Option (b). C and D both have 6 valence electrons, so same group.

questions.question:
The table below shows the electronic arrangements of six atoms, A to F.
Atom: A, B, C, D, E, F
Electronic configuration: 2,5 | 2 | 2,6 | 2,8,6 | 2,8,8 | 2,8,3
With respect to the table select the following:
(ii) Two noble gases:
questions.solution: Option (c). B (duplet, helium) and E (octet) have complete outer shells.

questions.question:
The table below shows the electronic arrangements of six atoms, A to F.
Atom: A, B, C, D, E, F
Electronic configuration: 2,5 | 2 | 2,6 | 2,8,6 | 2,8,8 | 2,8,3
With respect to the table select the following:
(iii) The atom which is the most electronegative:
questions.solution: Option (c). C (2,6) is the most electronegative of the options: electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group (B is a noble gas).

questions.question:
The table below shows the electronic arrangements of six atoms, A to F.
Atom: A, B, C, D, E, F
Electronic configuration: 2,5 | 2 | 2,6 | 2,8,6 | 2,8,8 | 2,8,3
With respect to the table select the following:
(iv) The atom which has the highest ionization potential:
questions.solution: Option (b). Atom B (2, helium) has the highest ionization potential: small size and complete duplet make removal of an electron very hard. NOTE: the printed key says (d) but its own explanation refers to atom B, which is option (b); correct answer is (b), printed key (d) is an error (accept either).
